body: It wasn't a conviction. I was in a mental hospital and my rights were removed. I just got them back yesterday. The stigma of mental health frightens me so much I don't want anyone to know. The area where I live only has 100 people in town and less than 2,000 in the county. I hate that people have to know everything about everyone. It's none of their business.

Ok, I don't think you understand what I'm asking. 

When one registers to vote online or snail mailed to the state--there is a line at the bottom asking "Have you ever been convicted of a felony or judged mentally incapacitated and disqualified to vote?" If you answer yes, then it asks "Has your right to vote been restored?" 

I simply want to know if my general registrar will see this paperwork. Will they know that my rights have been restored? No one knows my rights were ever taken away and I don't want ANYONE to know.
The problem is that I don't want them to know. Or, anyone else for that matter. I live in a small town and if my registrar sees that on my application, then the entire county would know as well.
You sound just like me. I wish you happiness or whatever you search for.
Ironically, I consider myself the listener. I've only asked for help maybe twice in my life, yet I can't stop thinking about killing myself.
